title: Quentin and the Extraction
premise: Odile Crane, a financial-crimes investigator haunted by a botched operation that cost his partner's life, receives a calendar invite from a handler who died six months ago — and when he arrives, he's pulled into an active extraction of Sable Voss, a defector carrying proof that the agency launders its own black budget through the very accounts Odile polices. As they run from hunters who seem to anticipate every move, Odile realizes the dead handler engineered this meeting deliberately: Sable is both the bait to expose the corruption and the only witness who can clear Odile's name in his partner's death. In the end, Odile must choose between delivering Sable to safety and broadcasting the ledger himself — he does both, burning his career, and the two escape into anonymity together, trading duty for each other.
about_author: Xanthe Vasquez is the pen name of a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing money she was never allowed to talk about. She writes thrillers from a coastal town where, she insists, nothing laundered ever washes ashore.

chapters.title: The Invitation from a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Insomniac Odile Crane audits clean money by day and replays the incident by night — until a calendar invite arrives from Handler Marcus Reeve, dead six months, for tomorrow at 9 a.m. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into compulsion; he decides to go.

chapters.title: Nine O'Clock, Room 414
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The hotel room is mid-operation: a woman code-named Sable Voss is being extracted while Reeve's voice plays from a laptop on a loop. Gunmen breach early. Odile grabs Sable on instinct. Beat: adrenaline replacing grief.

chapters.title: The Defector Who Knew His Name
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She doesn't trust her rescuer but knows his file cold — including the incident that broke him. She tests him with a detail only Reeve could have given her. Beat: wary alliance forged under fire.

chapters.title: Clean Money, Dirty Hands
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Hiding in a laundromat basement, Sable shows him shell-company ledgers routing agency black budget through accounts Odile himself once flagged and was ordered to close. Beat: his professional world tilts; the order came from above.

chapters.title: Hunters Who Move Like Insiders
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The pursuit team anticipates their safehouse before they reach it — someone inside is feeding coordinates. They split a burner phone and a lie. Beat: paranoia becomes the fifth character.

chapters.title: What Marcus Left in the Mail
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A dead-drop key Reeve mailed before dying yields a half-encrypted drive and a note: 'She's the bait. So are you.' Beat: Odile realizes the invitation was never accidental.

chapters.title: The Incident, Retold
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She reveals the official record of the incident was doctored — Odile's partner died because someone sold the op, not because Odile hesitated. Beat: guilt reframed as manipulation; rage replaces shame.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile reaches his old mentor, Deputy Director Halloran, offering the drive in exchange for protection. Halloran agrees too quickly. Beat: hope laced with the first real doubt.

chapters.title: The Exchange That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The handoff at a rail yard turns into an ambush; Halloran's men shoot first. Sable pulls Odile out wounded. Beat: betrayal confirmed; no institution left to trust.

chapters.title: Fever Logic
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Tending Odile's fever in a farmhouse, Sable decrypts more of the drive and finds footage of Reeve alive after his reported death. Beat: tenderness growing between them amid the revelation.

chapters.title: The Ghost Handler
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Following the footage, they find Reeve living off-grid — faked death to finish the investigation from outside. He admits he used Odile as bait to draw out the mole. Beat: fury, then grudging understanding.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Accounts
chapters.summary: Reeve's POV (single chapter). Reeve explains the architecture: twenty-two accounts, one per conspirator, and the drive holds all of it — but broadcasting it requires a live authentication only Sable can provide, which paints a target on her forever. Beat: the true cost named aloud.

chapters.title: The Mole Has a Face
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Cross-referencing account activity, Sable identifies the insider feeding the hunters: Halloran's aide, Wren — and evidence Halloran signed the order that doomed Odile's partner. Beat: vengeance within reach, dangerously tempting.

chapters.title: Bait Taken
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. They let themselves be tracked to a decoy location, feeding Wren false drive details to confirm the leak. The trap works — and traps them too. Beat: pyrrhic cleverness; capture imminent.

chapters.title: Interrogation of the Investigator
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Captured and pressed by Halloran to sign off on a cover story, Odile stalls using audit tricks, buying hours while Sable, free, moves on the broadcast site. Beat: duty weaponized against its own believer.

chapters.title: What Love Costs After Midnight
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. At the transmission node, Sable faces the choice Reeve warned of: authenticate and become hunted for life, or walk away rich and safe. She thinks of Odile. Beat: love against duty made literal.

chapters.title: The Ledger Goes Loud
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Sable authenticates; the ledger floods every financial-crimes desk in three governments. Simultaneously Odile escapes during the resulting chaos. Beat: catharsis — the truth finally louder than the guns.

chapters.title: Halloran's Last Audit
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile confronts Halloran with the signed order killing his partner, choosing arrest over execution, letting the system he still believes in devour its own. Beat: justice without satisfaction; closure earned.

chapters.title: Wren in the Wire
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Wren, cornered, tries to bargain with Sable's old identity — revealing Sable defected partly to escape her own crimes. Sable refuses the deal. Beat: identity confronted; the past declined.

chapters.title: Extraction, Reversed
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Officially disgraced and unofficially cleared, Odile is offered reinstatement if he disavows the broadcast. He declines, walking out of the building that defined him. Beat: duty released, self reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Meeting Neither Was Invited To
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Odile and Sable meet at the same hotel, room 414, now just a room. No handlers, no ledgers — two people deciding what remains when the mission ends. Beat: quiet intimacy; the beginning chosen freely.

chapters.title: Quentin and the Extraction
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, epilogue. Months later, under new names — she calls him Quentin now — they read news of the prosecutions unfolding. A stranger watches them from across the café; Sable notices, smiles, and takes Quentin's hand anyway. Beat: peace that stays vigilant; love that survived the bait.
